rKung Fu PandaEvery bowl made by hand.Plus dumplings.Every recipe serves 4.
    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersTraining bowl dumplingsShifu makes Po fight for the last oneHow to make it400g pork mince2 cups finely shredded wombok1 tbsp grated ginger2 spring onions, chopped30 dumpling wrappers4 tbsp soy sauce2 tbsp black vinegar1 tbsp chilli oilMix the pork with the wombok, ginger and spring onions and season.Fold spoonfuls into the wrappers, sealing the edges with water.Steam in batches over simmering water until cooked through.Mix the soy, black vinegar and chilli oil for dipping.Oogway's peachesFrom the tree where Oogway sitsHow to make it4 ripe peaches200g ricotta3 tbsp honey1/4 tsp ground cinnamon40g almonds, crushedHalve and stone the peaches.Grill the peaches cut side down until caramelised.Whip the ricotta with a spoon of honey and the cinnamon, then serve with the peaches, more honey and the almonds.Mr Ping's red bean steamed bunsStacked high, worth the climbHow to make it300g plain flour7g dried yeast40g caster sugar1 tsp baking powdersalt, a pinch160ml milk, warm1 tbsp vegetable oil250g red bean pasteMix the flour, yeast, caster sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl, then add the warm milk and oil and bring together into a dough.Knead for 8 minutes until smooth.Cover and prove in a warm spot for 1 hour.Divide into 12, flatten each piece, fill with a tablespoon of red bean paste and pinch closed. Sit each bun on a square of baking paper in a bamboo steamer.Cover and prove the buns for another 20 minutes.Steam over boiling water for 12 minutes and serve hot, stacked in the steamer.MainsSecret ingredient soupMr Ping's famous noodle soupHow to make it1kg chicken frames1 knob ginger, sliced4 garlic cloves1 bunch spring onions3 L water3 tbsp soy sauce1/2 tsp white pepper400g fresh egg noodles1 bunch bok choy300g chicken thigh filletsPut the frames in a pot with the ginger, garlic and spring onions and cover with the water.Simmer gently for 3 hours, skimming now and then, then strain. Poach the chicken thighs in the stock for the last 15 minutes.Season the stock with soy and white pepper and shred the chicken.Cook the noodles and bok choy briefly, then pour the hot stock over them with the chicken. The secret is there isn't one.Valley of Peace kung pao chickenThe busy village below the Jade PalaceHow to make it300g jasmine rice800g chicken thigh fillets, diced4 tbsp soy sauce1 tbsp cornflour, for the chicken1 tsp cornflour, for the sauce2 tbsp black vinegar1 tbsp caster sugar8 dried chillies1 tsp Sichuan peppercorns2 tbsp vegetable oil3 garlic cloves20g ginger4 spring onions80g roasted peanutsRinse the jasmine rice, then simmer covered in 450ml water on low for 15 minutes and rest off the heat.Toss the chicken with 1 tbsp of the soy sauce and the 1 tbsp cornflour for the chicken. Mix the remaining 3 tbsp soy, the black vinegar, sugar, the cornflour for the sauce and 60ml water for the sauce.Slice the garlic, grate the ginger and cut the spring onions into 3cm lengths.Heat the oil in a wok until very hot, stir-fry the dried chillies and Sichuan peppercorns for 20 seconds, then add the chicken and cook for 5 minutes.Add the garlic, ginger and spring onion, then the sauce, and toss until glossy. Stir in the peanuts and serve with the rice.SweetsAlmond cookiesThe Furious Five's training snackHow to make it125g butter120g caster sugar120g almond meal120g plain flour16 whole almonds1 egg, beatenBeat the butter and sugar, then mix in the almond meal and flour.Roll into 16 balls, press an almond on each and brush with egg.Bake at 170°C until golden.DrinksOogway's iced peach jasmine teaA quiet moment in the Jade PalaceHow to make it4 jasmine green tea bags1 L water at 80C3 ripe peaches, 2 for the puree and 1 for slices2 tbsp honey1 lemon, half juiced1 bag iceSteep the tea bags in the water for 3 minutes, remove and chill.Blend two peeled peaches with the honey and lemon juice until smooth.Stir the puree into the cold tea and pour over ice with thin peach slices.
